findings: Observed both the actual new painted master and the unchanged-size OLD/V7/BATTLE comparison. The native green reservoirs and plum cloth now agree with the selected battle subject; ochre worn coat, brown satchel, dark bun, human face and copper hooked staff remain recognizable.

The base face remains uncovered in the large and small portraits. The large portrait carries readable green/violet glass beside the shoulder; tiny vial and facial detail naturally compresses at32pixels, so no fine-detail claim is inferred from the enlarged master.

The map is a separate upright full figure with staff and green kit. The left encounter painting faces left with a raised hooked staff and the right painting faces right with an extended hooked staff; these are visibly distinct poses rather than a mirrored standing frame.

At the reviewed native size I see complete boots, equipment and staff silhouettes without an obvious neighboring-cell intrusion. Some contact antialiasing reaches the bottom canvas edge; this source review does not establish map-engine contact, animation timing or final gameplay rendering.

The coated-human silhouette remains close to its own upgrade by design; the upgrade separation relies on the mask, shoulder hoses and reinforced reservoir hardware. A final in-game pair comparison must judge that gap and compatibility with original HeroesIII lighting.

Observed both the actual new painted master and all five native outputs in the OLD/V7/BATTLE comparison. The same human woman, dark bun, worn ochre coat, satchel and hooked copper staff coherently match the new green/plum battle identity.

The fitted copper filter covers the lower face while keeping human eyes visible. Capped shoulder hoses and larger reinforced green reservoirs distinguish the upgrade from the uncovered base; the mask remains readable in the large portrait and forms a darker lower-face shape in the small portrait.

The separate map view stands with its staff and pressure kit. Left and right encounter views show genuinely different facing/body/weapon poses, with the left raised staff and the right extended hook. I see no ordinary ranged beam or extra gas-cloud effect.
Green liquid is concentrated in glass equipment, plum in cloth and fittings, and leather/copper/ochre remain physical materials. The whole body is not uniformly green and the human skin is preserved.

Native source suitability is positive, with no concrete subject clipping or cell-bleed blocker observed in the ten-output comparison. The same basic coat/body silhouette remains shared with the base; final art, native engine placement, gameplay and redistribution clearance remain pending.
